DharmaNexus identifies extensive text reuse between the *Navakapuggalapaññatti* and other Pali works, recording 784 matching passages across 37 texts [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Puggalapaññatti* itself, significant reuse occurs with the *Ekakapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.1, with its longest shared passage spanning §0.3–6.2 and §21.2–27.2_0), the *Catukkapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4), the *Tikapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.3), the *Dukapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.2), and the *Sattakapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.7) [DharmaNexus]. Sutta parallels include the *Kīṭāgiri Sutta* (MN 70, where segments §3.1–3.3 correspond to §15.1–15.3) and the *Catukkanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 4), alongside Abhidhamma links to the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 4.9) [DharmaNexus]. Passages are also shared widely with commentary and subcommentary literature, including the *Pāthikavagga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Majjhimapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Pañcakanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments computed by DharmaNexus link the text to the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26, e.g. §2.3–3.1 aligned with §0751b14_1–0751b15_1) and the Tibetan translation of the *Śrāvakabhūmi* in the *Yogācārabhūmi* (D 4036) [DharmaNexus].
